newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-DOULL GRABS 4-21 TO LEAD FIGHTBACK AGAINST PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DOULL GRABS 4-21 TO LEAD FIGHTBACK AGAINST PAKISTAN.

text.p: New Zealand, bundled out for 155 by Waqar Younis and Mushtaq Ahmed, hit back to leave Pakistan tottering on 52 for five at the close of an incident-packed opening day of the first test on Thursday.
Pace bowler Simon Doull led the New Zealand fightback by capturing four for 21 from seven destructive overs as the Pakistanis collapsed from 21 for no wicket to 37 for five at one stage.
When bad light halted play 10 overs early, Pakistan's last recognised batting pair of Salim Malik and wicketkeeper Moin Khan was together with 11 and five respectively.
The home side, whose captain Wasim Akram pulled out of the match because of sore shoulder, suffered their first setback when Doull bowled Saeed Anwar for eight at 21.
They lost Ijaz Ahmed at 29 when he was adjudged lbw to Chris Cairns by Zimbabwean umpire Russel Tiffin, who was standing in his first test abroad.
Ijaz, who made three, was visibly upset at the umpire's decision, saying the ball touched the bat before hitting the pads as he stretched forward.
Pakistan's woes continued with the dismissal of Inzamam-ul-Haq, who was returning to test cricket after knee surgery that forced him to miss the recent home series against Zimbabwe.

He was brilliantly taken at third slip without scoring by Nathan Astle, diving to his left, off Doull's bowling. Three runs later debutant Zahoor Elahi was caught by Stephen Fleming at first slip, having hit 22 off 26 balls, with a six and three fours.
Four balls later, Doull picked up his fourth wicket when Mohammad Wasim, also winning his first test cap, played on.
New Zealand, winning the toss and batting first, never really recovered from a poor start after openers Bryan Young and Justin Vaughan were back in the pavillion with 16 on the board.
Their innings was briefly revived by the third-wicket stand of 51 between Adam Parore, the highest scorer with 37, and Fleming, who made 19.
However, New Zealand crumbled after lunch when they lost the remaining seven wickets for 88, fast bowler Waqar finishing with four for 48 and leg-spinner Mushtaq capturing four for 59.
The final total was improved marginally by last-wicket pair Dipak Patel (26) and Doul (15 not out), who added 38.
